headlines.title: How Retirees Can Turn $300,000 Into Passive Income With These 4 High-Yield Stocks
headlines.summary: Selling shares in a downturn locks in losses a retiree can never earn back. Four dividend payers from four different sectors offer another route, and each one carries a payout test and a risk worth checking before you buy.

headlines.title: Is Altria Group (MO) Fully Valued As Higher EPS Guidance, A Dividend Hike, And Buybacks Lift Sentiment?
headlines.summary: Altria Group (MO) has investors refocusing on the stock after management raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance, lifted the quarterly dividend again, and approved an extra US$1b for share repurchases. Those moves came after a strong run in Altria Group’s share price, with a 90 day share price return of 17.31% and a year to date share price return of 35.16%. The 1 year total shareholder return of 40.31% and 5 year total shareholder return of 157.

headlines.title: A $300,000 Portfolio in Omega Healthcare, Edison International and Altria Pays $17,064 a Year in Dividends. Here’s What Happens if One Cuts
headlines.summary: Key TakeawaysA hypothetical $300,000 portfolio split evenly across Omega Healthcare, Edison International and Altria pays about $17,100 a year in dividends at today’s prices, or about $1,420 a month. Omega is the least covered of the three, paying out 91% of its AFFO in fiscal 2025, though consensus has that easing to 86% in fiscal 2026.

headlines.title: 5 Huge Dividend Payers the IRS Leaves Alone Inside a Roth
headlines.summary: Two investors can hold the exact same five blue chip dividend stocks and still walk away with very different paychecks. The difference comes down to one account choice, and over 20 years it snowballs into a six-figure surprise.

headlines.title: 4 High Yield Stocks That Have Never Missed a Dividend Payment
headlines.summary: Recessions, oil crashes, and a pandemic failed to interrupt the quarterly checks from four household-name payers. But an unbroken record is a lower bar than it sounds, so we stress-tested each one on cash flow and debt before trusting the next payment.

description: Altria Group, Inc., through its subsidiaries, manufactures and sells smokeable and oral tobacco products in the United States. It offers cigarettes primarily under the Marlboro brand; large cigars and pipe tobacco under the Black & Mild brand; moist smokeless tobacco and oral tobacco products under the Copenhagen, Skoal, Red Seal, and Husky brands; oral nicotine pouches under the on! brand; and e-vapor products under the NJOY ACE brand. The company sells its products to distributors, as well as large retail organizations, such as chain stores. Altria Group, Inc. was founded in 1822 and is headquartered in Richmond, Virginia.
